what: Suggested benchmark design for 8 barcoded organoids
title: Pseudo-bulk generation strategies for phenotype-guided single-cell benchmarking
text: Tip specific setting — approximately 20,000 single cells 8 barcoded organoids, four successful four failed differentiation outcomes — avoid relying single pseudo-bulk design. robust benchmark use three nested levels: Observed organoid pseudo-bulk Yb=∑c:b(c)=bxc Y_b=\sum_{c:b(c)=b}x_c gives 88 realistic pseudo-bulk samples. Organoid-preserving bootstraps Ybrboot=∑c∈𝒞brxc,𝒞br⊆{c:b(c)=b} Y_{br}^{\mathrm{boot}}=\sum_{c\\mathcal{C}_{br}}x_c, \qquad \mathcal{C}_{br}\subseteq\{c:b(c)=b\} gives technical replicates preserving barcode structure. Phenotype-stratified custom-composition simulations Yi=∑k=1K∑c∈𝒞ikxc,(Ni1,…,NiK)∼Multinomial(Ni,πi) Y_i=\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{c\\mathcal{C}_{ik}}x_c, \qquad (N_{i1},\ldots,N_{iK})\sim\mathrm{Multinomial}(N_i,\pi_i) creates controlled success/failure pseudo-bulk cohorts known ground truth.

title: Pseudo-bulk generation strategies for phenotype-guided single-cell benchmarking
text: single-cell expression vectors independent Gaussian, xc∼𝒩(μ,Σ), x_c\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu,\Sigma), aggregation simple: Yi=∑c=1Nixc∼𝒩(Niμ,NiΣ). Y_i=\sum_{c=1}^{N_i}x_c \sim \mathcal{N}(N_i\mu,N_i\Sigma). cells share organoid-level programs, Cov(xc,xc′)=C(c≠c′), \mathrm{Cov}(x_c,x_{c'})=C \quad (c\neq c'), Var(Yi)=NiΣ+Ni(Ni−1)C. \mathrm{Var}(Y_i) = N_i\Sigma + N_i(N_i-1)C. Ni(Ni−1)CN_i(N_i-1)C term means shared biological programs can dominate pseudo-bulk variance. Therefore, naïve aggregation can overstate biological signal many bootstraps reuse organoids. log-normal single-cell models, xc=exp⁡(zc),zc∼𝒩(μ,Σ), x_c=\exp(z_c),\qquad z_c\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu,\Sigma), sum Yi=∑cxc Y_i=\sum_c x_c exactly log-normal. Moment-matching Gaussian CLT approximations may used, sparse precision matrix inferred single-cell level generally preserved aggregation.

title: Hierarchical relative RMSE against a shared compositional reference — eval_hrRMSE
text: arranging data, sample \(\), cell type \(j\), measurement source \(m\): $$ y_{ijm} = \begin{cases} p_j, & m = \text{gold standard}, \\ \hat{p}_{ij}, & m = \text{estimated}. \end{cases} $$ hierarchical mixed-effects model : $$ y_{ijm} = \mu + \beta\, (m = \text{estimated}) + u_j + v_{ij} + \varepsilon_{ijm}, $$ $$u_j \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2_{\mathrm{population}}),$$ $$v_{ij} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2_{\mathrm{sample}}),$$ $$\varepsilon_{ijm} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_e^2).$$ Biological signal variance $$ V_T = \sigma^2_{\mathrm{population}} + \sigma^2_{\mathrm{sample}}, $$ $$ \mathrm{hrRMSE} = \sqrt{\frac{\sigma_e^2}{V_T}}. $$ Variance components estimated REML ML. Values 1 indicate residual disagreement smaller variance separating cell-type abundances.
